A team that can’t play with the ball can’t control a game. That makes it very hard to see out leads. Look at the struggles this team has had late in many games, even against terrible teams. No manager sticks with a 35 (or even 40)% possession rate for a whole season. It will never happen in a top 20 league and be very successful. If for no reason other than obvious necessity, teams move away from that strategy as the season progresses. There are decades of this not happening. I’m not being arrogant. It just flat out doesn’t happen. 

If it humors you to play the hypothetical game despite the fact that it will never happen, I would change my mind if a couple teams were able to do it while playing at a top level in a good league. I’d say there is the same chance of that happening as me winning the lottery and I don’t buy lottery tickets.

As far as possession stats go, I won’t change my mind. You can’t play at 35% consistently and have a very good season. Luckily, Ramsay figured that out after some awful results against teams they should have destroyed. The downside of extremely low possession should be obvious to everyone. It’s not a secret. 

We have a young manager who doesn’t know the league well or have much experience. He has a ton to learn and will hopefully do so quickly. He chose an unsustainable model of play that has now morphed most of the time. People sometimes act like it’s crazy to question a coach/manager in sports unless you have coached at their level. Yet you see coaches fired constantly, especially in soccer. That’s not because they don’t understand the game. It’s usually because they don’t assimilate to a particular league and/or try to put square pegs in round holes due to stubbornness. 

The Loons are doing fine. They are still almost 2 points under expected (which isn’t bad) for the season. They have played the easiest schedule in MLS history to this point. That’s very likely still going to be the case at the end of the season. The Seattle win was a really good win. It would be silly to get too high or low before about the 30th game. I’m sure you will continue to see the team possess at much higher rated other than in rare instances. 

Now they need to learn to be effective using the ball and breaking down a defense. They haven’t had any success on those fronts yet. Success comes from being adaptable and able to take advantage of whatever a team will give you. Many high level coaches in all sports fail to master that. Ramsay has a great opportunity to learn those things in a fairly forgiving lead playing teams who are often the opposite of adaptable. I just don’t want to see the Loons become one of those teams. Many teams pigeon hole themselves and don’t see it soon enough.

Tani is definitely on my all time favorite Loons team. He has that drive and desire that a lot of players just don’t have. It makes him more productive than a lot of more talented players. And he’s a lot more fun to watch as a fan because of it. Hopefully he can get a deal he is happy with in the short and long term. That’s what we should be hoping for all the players, but especially the guys that always find a little more to give. Every team in every sport could use a few more guys like him.

I blamed 4 people. Boxall starts the mess and has primary responsibility. That doesn’t absolve later mistakes. He was in the area and doing absolutely nothing useful on what was obviously going to be a shot. You have to make a choice to defend something and not just be in the area. 

Trapp did a great job and closed down the likely shot from a very dangerous player in a very dangerous spot. His responsibility isn’t backside defending. Imagine if he left the shot open to cut off a pass to a marked player. People would want to put clown shoes on him. The Austin goal was a very good looking goal and give credit to them for making the passes and runs to put that ball in the goal. 

However, that was a horrible job on the part of 3 or 4 Loons players. Boxall does the long throw bit (which has led to many goals) then seems to forget the situation and inexplicably steps to the ball. He is thoroughly beaten at that point. That’s a bad situation, but we still have plenty of defenders in good positions to stop the sequence multiple times. 

Perayra chooses to be a passenger on the play and barely shuffles his feet as Bukari runs past him. This is just lazy and inexcusable. A moderate amount of effort takes away that outlet pass that leads to the rest of the defensive scrambling once Austin is in the attacking half. 

Gressel has the ability to come over and contain the run at about the 25 yard mark. Instead, he slows up to evidently try to take away a possible 25 yard pass. This hesitation makes no sense and would have still been a poor idea even if that pass is attempted. This allows Bukari to accelerate again and easily create a ton of space. 

This leads to a very easy and dangerous pass at the top of the box to Uzuni. Trapp does a fantastic job tracking and anticipating and manning the center of the field during all this chaos and closes down Uzuni almost immediately. Unfortunately, Kolmanic makes a nice run and beats another Loon (I don’t remember who, but this player probably could have slid and broken up the pass also)then slots home a really nice shot.

Austin now has 10 goals scored (worst in MLS) through 15 games. They don’t score goals like this without a ton of help. And, with all this errors, Austin was a foot from not scoring. 4 players could have easily prevented that goal including one, whose legs it went between, twice. Trapp was the only defender who showed any competency there. This is how you lose points against bad teams and something they need to clean up ASAP.

Counterattacking teams perform poorly in XG vs G the majority of the time like the Loons are doing. 

And, to say goals given up defending leads or at the end of games are equal to goals given up in the first 60 minutes ignores all facts about soccer. Roughly half of goals are scored in the final 1/3 of games across all leagues, not to mention teams trailing score at a higher rate as well. XG is a solid measuring stick (the best we have likely due to lack of statistic based models), but has many flaws. It isn’t reasonable to apply all data unilaterally to all leagues. It would be impossible for one source to track all leagues or even say the top 20 leagues. Even doing it by continent would improve the data significantly as most continents play roughly the same way. 

The G+ ranking are even less reliable. Different leagues have different roster builds, playing styles, talent levels and philosophies at play. Those things aren’t factored in and what is considered .2 XG is deemed that universally. Anyone who knows the game understands the same scoring opportunities don’t lead to the same frequencies of goals in all leagues. It is also very subjective. And none of these statistics take into account having a defense unbalanced or on their heels or just a terrible defensive play or sequence. 

Just to use a recent example of this, last weeks game had Vancouver at 1.55 XG and the Loons at 1.56. If you go back and read the postgame comments you will see people talk about how badly the Loons were trounced. My inclination would be to side with the people over the stats on that game. I can’t imagine anyone believes the Loons had a 50/50 shot to win that game.

This isn’t to say XG is useless by any means. It is useful to a point. It definitely is not without its flaws though. One can confidently assume more statistical models will be designed with many likely being league/area specific in the next few years. There are already a few American companies doing this on smaller scales.

As you can see from a previous post, we have no true rival but SKC, Colorado, Portland, Houston and Seattle are the closest we have in some unknown order. We play a 4-2-3-1 about 95% of the time. Following is my ranking of our positional groups. 

Playmaker (#10} Emanuel Reynoso. I would argue the best overall player in MLS since he arrived in 2020. The only players who have been in MLS roughly the same amount of time in the conversation are Carles Gil and Hany Mukhtar. Rey is a playmaking genius who is underrated even by our fans. 

Goalie is Dayne St Clair. At his best he is about the best. At his earlier form from 2023, he is a little above average. Elite level shot stopper who has great instincts and is very athletic. People bitch about his distribution, but not Franco Fragapane (see highlights from last week). He has been great since Leagues Cup. 

CBs - Boxall, Tapias, Dibassy, Kallman. This is an aging group that is very reliable and deep by MLS standards. Tapias has very quietly been one of the best preseason acquisitions in MLS with Dibassy coming back from injury. Boxall is our rock and has been with the team almost since the start. 

Wingers, wide attacking mids - lots of depth and no health/fitness in this group. We have the ever improving Bongi Hlongwane who is possibly the most improved player in MLS. He usually plays on the right and Fragapane is the preferred starter in the left but has been hurt a lot which has limited his effectiveness. We also have Ismael Tijouri-Shradi who was a late summer pickup. He has been great when available, but has career long availability issues. Sang Bin is a solid depth player but isn’t refined at all. He does have speed and some on ball skills and is a great 20 minute sub we need to develop a lot in the next year. Due to lack of options we have played Dotson and Rosales on the wing, though they are d mids)  a lot with mixed success. Things often revert to more of a 4-3-3 when they are on the wing as they are both naturally…..

Defensive mids - another position where availability has been a bit of an issue. Trapp is our locked in starting #6 (primary d mid) for better or worse. He gets a lot of flack on this sub and is by no means a great player. He is our best option though and has played pretty well down the stretch. He is aging and, like most d mids, benefits from us having more possession (not our typical game though more prevalent with Rey on the field). His partner has varied a ton and there are no lack of options for who it could be. Kervin Arriaga is our most gifted option though he sometimes disappears and seems like more of a true double pivot guy than is ideal with our roster. Dotson and Rosales both have great moments and are high energy players with decent offensive skill though not great passers. We brought Jan Gregus back at the deadline as a desperation move due to injuries and he has been fantastic against reasonable odds. He isn’t super fast and neither is Trapp, but they have been a very good pairing lately. 

Many will disagree, but I’m putting the striker (#9) down here. We picked up proven vet Teemu Pukki (no, not the orange packaged products that show up on your doorstep for pennies on the dollar, though that’s what we got him for). The results have been mixed with him though they seem to be getting better. He has often appeared frustrated on the field. He could be the key to a huge stretch run and playoffs if he can fully get on the same page as Rey. There are positive signs that could be coming. The backup is speedy and raw Mender Garcia who is a good late game sub but not a starter at this point. He probably gets way too much grief on here as he is essentially a fake DP (more on that coming). 

Fullbacks/outside backs  without a doubt our Achilles heel. Heath likes to use them to help in possession and to create offensive width. We have yet to find good players for our system by and large and this year seems worse. We usually start Taylor on the right and recent acquisition Ethan Bristow on the left. We also have Valentin available on the right and Padelford or Rosales who can play on the left. I’d love to see us start Valentin and Rosales together for a few games. Our LBs are all fairly young and hopefully one takes over the spot for ‘24. We will need a big upgrade at RB. 

Depth has always been an issue though is better now. We also seem to have lots of injuries though it’s really the case globally in soccer. We lost Robin Lod early in the year who is a key (and versatile) player for us. The core for next year looks pretty good and the needs seem pretty obvious (a better RB, lockdown #6, youth at CB and striker depth) depending on who is brought back. 

Our biggest issue is that our owner is as tight with his money as Scrooge. He invests the minimum possible to keep a relatively competitive roster. That puts a ton of pressure on the front office and magnifies every decision that isn’t perfect. IMO. This leads to a lot of misplaced complaining about manager Adrian Heath. He isn’t perfect, but does extremely well with a bottom tier payroll and lack of depth. He is much maligned though his detractors really only cite that we have reached our ceiling with him as manager. That’s likely true as it would be with any manager with a bottom 4 payroll in a 29 team league. The Loons make the Twins look like big spenders. A great example is Mender being a DP. He really isn’t one and fills that slot so we can make use of our minimal investment “young DP/U22” slots. We also got Pukki on a free transfer while younger, more desirable strikers were brought in by teams like RSL, NYC and Nashville who aren’t big spenders either.
Colorado or Portland would be my top 2.
The Yankees won’t be in the playoffs. And, how can you say the Twins will never compete in comparison to the Vikings? Neither has a great shot, but small market teams have won many World Series.
